claims.statement: `Institution.csv_format` on `account_institutions` is a comma-separated positional template string mapping each column of a broker CSV export to a standardized placeholder, and it is the only per-broker configuration the generic parser consumes — there is no broker-specific branching in `src/account/csv/parser.py`.

`normalize_token` is the single normalization rule applied to both template tokens and file headers — it strips a leading UTF-8 BOM and whitespace, unwraps `{...}`, lowercases, and collapses non-alphanumeric runs into single underscores — so real-world broker labels only match the template through the `HEADER_ALIASES` table.

`header_matches` accepts a header alias match in either direction (actual in `HEADER_ALIASES[expected]` or expected in `HEADER_ALIASES[actual]`), which is what lets a `{type}` template token line up with a file column labeled `Security Type`.

Header validation is two-stage and strictly positional: a raw column-count mismatch raises `CsvHeaderCountMismatchError` before any name comparison, and the first element-wise name mismatch raises `CsvHeaderColumnMismatchError` with a 1-based column index; a reordered export therefore fails even when every label is recognized.

`map_account_type` lowercases and trims the raw account type and resolves only the documented `ACCOUNT_TYPE_MAP` keys (TFSA/RRSP/FHSA variants plus non-registered/personal/margin) to `AccountTypeEnum`; an unrecognized value raises `CsvUnsupportedAccountTypeError` and aborts the entire parse rather than skipping the row.

`_parse_position` treats quantity and book value asymmetrically: an unparseable quantity raises `CsvInvalidQuantityError` (and a missing quantity cell silently parses as `Decimal("0")`), while an unparseable book value is swallowed into `None` so a malformed cost basis degrades to unknown cost instead of failing the import.

`calculate_average_cost` returns `None` for non-positive quantity or missing book value, otherwise quantizes `book_value / quantity` to 4 decimal places with `ROUND_HALF_UP`; that quantize step fixes every CSV-imported `average_cost` and cascades into all downstream cost-basis P&L.

`GenericCsvParser.parse` enforces per-row invariants while grouping by `account_number`: every row needs a non-empty account number (`CsvMissingAccountNumberError`), but only the first row seen for a new account number needs a non-empty account type (`CsvMissingAccountTypeError`); accounts are returned in first-seen order with `row_idx` reported as a 1-based file line number starting at 2.

Row filtering runs before the quantity parse in `_parse_position`: cash rows (empty symbol, `cash` symbol or security_type, or a `sec-c-` prefix) and option rows (OCC-pattern symbols via `OCC_OPTION_PATTERN`, or `option`/`derivative` security types) are dropped and never become positions or raise quantity errors; options are defended a second time in `sync_account_csv_positions` via `is_option_symbol`.

The parser's exception taxonomy is rooted at `CsvParserError` with three branches — `CsvHeaderValidationError` (count/column), `CsvEmptyError` (empty content, empty template, no columns; plus the service-level `CsvFileEmptyError` subclass), and `CsvRowValidationError` (unsupported account type, missing account number, missing account type, invalid quantity) — and the router maps `CsvParserError` to HTTP 400 with the message as `detail`.

All three CSV endpoints (`POST /accounts/csv/inspect`, `/accounts/csv/import`, `/accounts/{account_id}/csv-sync`) share one gate: `CsvAccountService.validate_csv_institution` raises `InstitutionNotFoundError` (404) when the institution row is missing and `CsvImportDisabledError` (400) when `csv_import_enabled` is false OR `csv_format` is empty, so `csv_import_enabled=True` with `csv_format=None` behaves identically to a disabled institution.

`inspect_csv` parses, then when a `user_id` is given it marks `exists = True` and overwrites each discovered account's currency with the stored `Account.currency` for account numbers the user already has at that institution; `exists` drives the modal's `Update holdings` versus `Create account` badge.

`import_accounts` filters parsed accounts against the requested `account_numbers` and raises `NoMatchingAccountsInCsvError` when the intersection is empty — there is no import-everything mode. `CsvAccountDuplicateError` is mapped to 400 by the router but is never raised on this path: a requested number that already exists is treated as an in-place update returning the same account id.

Accounts created by CSV import are stamped `api_sync_enabled=False` (with `integration_user_id=None`), which is what makes the broker sync path refuse them and makes the frontend account-row refresh control render `Update from CSV` instead of `Sync positions`.

Currency resolution at import has a defined precedence per account: the caller-supplied `account_currencies[number]` (trimmed and uppercased) wins, then the parsed account currency, then `"CAD"`; for an existing account a difference triggers `AccountRepository.update_currency`, and for a new account it becomes the `AccountSchema.currency`.

`sync_account_from_csv` is asymmetric with import: it never creates an account, never changes the account currency, and never considers other discovered accounts in the file — it matches only the target account's `external_id` (raising `AccountNotInCsvError` otherwise), validates the account's own institution's CSV enablement, and is the only CSV endpoint that enforces account ownership (404 for another user's account).

`sync_account_csv_positions` is the shared tail for all three paths: it resolves each symbol through `SecurityApi.get_or_create_from_broker` (wrapping a `ValueError` from the market layer as `SecurityResolutionError`, which the router maps to 400), then writes via `PositionApi.create` — which replaces every position row for the account — or calls `sync_by_account(account_id, [])` when the resolved list is empty, so an all-cash export clears the account instead of leaving stale rows; finally it stamps `update_last_sync_at`.

Security resolution for CSV positions is institution-scoped and cached through `SecurityBroker` rows: a repeat `(institution, broker_symbol, broker_exchange)` short-circuits to the mapped security, and a new pair maps the broker symbol/exchange to an EODHD query (`TSX`→`TO`, `CSE`→`CA`, `NYSE`/`NASDAQ`→`US`, `.`→`-`), searches the cached gateway, creates or reuses the security, primes its latest close, and records the raw search results.

The CSV endpoints accept `institution_id`, `account_numbers` and `currencies` as either multipart form fields or query parameters with the same alias (form wins); `institution_id` and `account_numbers` are mandatory (422), account numbers accept a JSON list string, a comma-separated string, or repeated values and are deduplicated in order, and a malformed `currencies` JSON is silently ignored rather than rejected.
None of the three CSV endpoints carries a rate limit — only `POST /accounts/{account_id}/sync` is decorated with `@limiter.limit("3/minute")` in `src/account/router.py`.

All three CSV endpoints decode the upload with `content_bytes.decode("utf-8-sig")`, so a UTF-8 BOM never reaches the parser and a read/decode failure produces an HTTP 400 rather than an unhandled 500; the parser additionally strips a leading BOM defensively.

`WEALTHSIMPLE_CSV_FORMAT` in `src/commands/seed.py` is the worked example of the template contract: 21 placeholders in Wealthsimple column order, seeded onto the `WEALTHSIMPLE` institution with `csv_import_enabled=True` and re-asserted on every seed run for an already-existing institution, so a template change reaches an existing database.

Onboarding a new broker CSV export is a data change, not a code change: set `csv_format` to the positional template matching the export header and `csv_import_enabled = True`; parser code only needs touching when the export requires placeholder vocabulary the parser does not consume or a header label no alias covers. The caveat is that templates omitting `{account_number}` or `{account_type}` fail at runtime with the row-level missing errors, and omitting `{quantity}` silently yields zero-quantity positions.

The institution seam surfaces to the frontend through `GET /integration/institutions`, which returns `csv_import_enabled` and `csv_format`; the import modal filters that list to `csv_import_enabled === true` and auto-selects the broker when exactly one remains, so adding a second CSV broker requires no frontend change.

`import-account-csv-modal.svelte` is a two-step dialog (broker+file, then a preview table) with client-side `.csv`-extension and 10 MB size guards that disable the primary button, an empty-account-list error that keeps the user on step 1, all discovered accounts selected by default with select-all/indeterminate header state, per-row currency dropdowns, and `Back` preserving the broker and file.

`update-account-csv-modal.svelte` is a single-step dialog that sends only the file for one account to `syncAccountCsv(account.id, file)` — no institution or account number travels in the body; it is opened from the account-row refresh control that renders `Update from CSV` when `api_sync_enabled` is false.

`AccountClient.importAccountsCsv`'s fourth parameter is overloaded as `currenciesOrToken?: Record<string,string> | string | null`: a string is routed to the auth token while an object becomes the stringified `currencies` form field, and the client sends repeated `account_numbers` fields.

Both CSV modals render the backend `detail` string verbatim in a destructive alert, so the parser's diagnostic messages (column index, expected and actual header names, row index, symbol, account type) are what end users actually read.

Focused CSV coverage is layered: `tests/account/csv/test_parser.py` pins the template/alias/filter/rounding contract, `tests/services/test_csv_account_service.py` pins the institution gate and the create/update/sync branches with mocked repositories and `SecurityApi`, `tests/routers/test_csv_inspect.py` and `tests/routers/test_csv_account_endpoints.py` drive the real FastAPI app against Postgres asserting status codes and `PositionModel` rows, and `tests/commands/test_seed.py` pins the seeded template plus seed idempotency.
